data.narrative:
Dexterity is a Series B robotics and manufacturing company founded by Samir Menon, Robert Sun, Kevin Chavez, and others. The company raised $291M to reach a current post-money valuation of $1.65B. The valuation analysis draws on a comparable universe of 9 private peers and 1 public company in robotics and manufacturing, including Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B Series B), Generalist AI ($2.0B Series B), Hadrian ($1.6B Series C), Agile Robots ($1.0B Series C), and Nimble Robotics ($1.0B Series C).

Two valuation methods triangulate Dexterity's fair value. The peer-median approach across 5 same-sector peers at the same or adjacent stage yields $1.6B, reflecting a range of $1.0B to $2.0B. The stage-progression method applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B advancement, deriving an implied valuation of $3.1B from the current $1.6B post-money base.

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $1.4B (low) to $3.6B (high), with a median of $2.4B. The wide spread reflects tension between peer comparability—which clusters near the current valuation—and forward-stage progression expectations. Key uncertainties include the timing and terms of the next financing round, the trajectory of revenue relative to competitors, and sector-wide momentum in autonomous manufacturing.
